staticMarkdownSelectors.target: 丘 means a hill or knoll
matches: 丘 means a hill or knoll: land rising above its surroundings. The native noun is 丘 おか. A hill is typically lower and gentler than a mountain, but these everyday labels do not impose a universal numerical height boundary.

Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology: Imagine the short slant and upright strokes as a small rise standing on the long ground line. This is a visual memory aid, not a historical explanation of the character.

staticMarkdownSelectors.target: not exact synonyms or a set of antonyms
matches: 丘 (おか) is a hill without specifying its material. 砂 (すな) is the sand itself, not the landform. 砂漠 (さばく) is a desert region, not an individual dune; a desert need not be covered in dunes. 砂浜 (すなはま) is a sandy beach. These are related geographical words, not exact synonyms or a set of antonyms.
